adds.title: Ceará Law No. 17,480
adds.summary: Ceará Law No. 17,480 sanctioned by Governor Camilo Santana and published 19 May 2021 requires public and private establishments, effective 90 days after publication, to affix a visible minimum 50 cm by 50 cm notice on the exterior or at an entrance stating discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity is expressly prohibited and listing the Special Coordination for LGBT Public Policies phone for complaints, clarifications and reports.

adds.title: Supreme Federal Court ruling on gender identity
adds.summary: In 2018 in ADI 4275 Brazil's Supreme Federal Court recognized gender identity/expression as protected under equality and allowed alteration of name and gender in the civil registry without sex-reassignment surgery or judicial authorization; in ADO 26 and MI 4733 it equated transfobia and homofobia to the crime of racism until Congress enacts specific criminal legislation; in 2024 in ADI 5668 interpreting the National Education Plan (Law 13.005/2014) it imposed on public and private schools a duty to combat discrimination based on gender, gender identity and sexual orientation; in ADPF 787 it required the Unified Health System (SUS) to guarantee transsexual and travesti persons full access to health services matching their biological apparatus and physiological needs; in precautionary decision in ADPF 527 it ordered transfer of transsexual women inmates to women's prisons, followed by a National Justice Council resolution requiring a judge to set detention location after asking the detained person's preference, in a context where Brazil leads global violence against transgender persons with average life expectancy around 30 years versus ~75 nationally.

adds.title: Court of Justice of Ceará (TJCE) decision on Brune Bonassi
adds.summary: Ceará will issue its first birth certificate recognizing a person as non-binary.

adds.title: Sobral City Council bill on gender issues in schools
adds.summary: On 12 December 2017 the Sobral (CE) Municipal Chamber approved Bill No. 2154/17, authored by Councillor Adauto Izidoro Arruda, prohibiting pedagogical activities reproducing the concept of "gender ideology" / any discussion of gender diversity in all municipal and private schools in Sobral by majority vote with the sole opposing vote from Councillor Maria Socorro Brasileiro Magalhães, forwarding the bill to Mayor Ivo Gomes to sanction or veto.
